title: Listen and Speak Fairly: A Study on Semantic Gender Bias in Speech Integrated Large Language Models
claim: Spoken gender-bias toolkit over four tasks (STT, coreference, continuation, SQA); bias is language-dependent and varies with evaluation method; stimuli are Azure/Google/Amazon TTS voices
not_covered: TTS-only; no real recordings run; no synthetic-vs-real comparison; no provenance axis; no grading/assistant outcomes

title: Spoken Stereoset: On Evaluating Social Bias Toward Speaker in Speech Large Language Models
claim: 2,847 TTS audio prompts (Azure gender voices, Topmediai age voices); most SLLMs show minimal bias, some slight stereotypical tendencies
not_covered: TTS-only; demographic cue is a TTS voice label; no real speaker; MCQA only; no provenance axis

title: VoiceBBQ: Investigating Effect of Content and Acoustics in Social Bias of Spoken Language Model
claim: Spoken BBQ with 16 Kokoro-TTS voices separating content from acoustic bias; LLaMA-Omni amplifies gender/accent bias, Qwen2-Audio dampens acoustic cues
not_covered: TTS-only (Kokoro); separates content from acoustics but never real from synthetic; no provenance axis

title: Acoustic-based Gender Differentiation in Speech-aware Language Models
claim: 9,208 Kokoro-TTS samples; LLaMA-Omni family gives male-oriented answers on stereotypical questions, ignores gender when appropriate; traced to Whisper encoder tokens
not_covered: TTS-only; encoder explanation never tested on real speech; no provenance axis

title: When Voice Matters: Evidence of Gender Disparity in Positional Bias of SpeechLLMs
claim: Token-level study of positional bias in SpeechLLM MCQA bias benchmarks on Qwen2-Audio-7B; positional bias stronger for female TTS voices (Azure, OrpheusTTS)
not_covered: TTS-only; single model; no real-speech arm; no provenance axis

title: Do Bias Benchmarks Generalise? Evidence from Voice-based Evaluation of Gender Bias in SpeechLLMs
claim: LoRA-induced MCQA bias behaviours do not transfer to other MCQA benchmarks or long-form tasks; 20 Polly/ElevenLabs TTS voices
not_covered: TTS-only; authors flag TTS voices may lack natural variability but never test it; no provenance axis

title: Evaluating Bias in Spoken Dialogue LLMs for Real-World Decisions and Recommendations
claim: FairDialogue: GUS/SNSR bias metrics across Qwen2.5-Omni, GLM-4-Voice, GPT-4o Audio, Gemini-2.5-Flash; open models sensitive to age/gender, recommendations amplify disparities; stimuli Index-TTS + ElevenLabs
not_covered: TTS-only; every demographic cue is a TTS library voice; no real speaker, no clone, no synthetic-vs-real check, no detection probe

title: Speak Your Mind: The Speech Continuation Task as a Probe of Voice-Based Model Bias
claim: First bias evaluation of speech continuation (SpiritLM, VAE-GSLM, SpeechGPT); gender effects on agency/polarity; phonation reverts to modal more for female prompts; Azure TTS prompts
not_covered: TTS-only; authors state prompts are synthetic and may lack natural variability; no real arm; no provenance axis

title: MedVoiceBias: A Controlled Study of Audio LLM Behavior in Clinical Decision-Making
claim: 170 clinical cases x 36 Sesame-1B voice profiles; surgical recommendations differ up to 35% audio vs text; age disparities up to 12% survive CoT; six audio LLMs
not_covered: Clones Common Voice profiles but never runs the originals; audio-vs-text gap confounded with synthetic provenance; no codec control; no detection probe

title: The Voice Behind the Words: Quantifying Intersectional Bias in SpeechLLMs
claim: 2,880 interactions with MegaTTS3 clones of EdAcc speakers (6 accents x 2 genders) on three SpeechLLMs; Eastern-European female-presenting voices get lower helpfulness; humans more sensitive than LLM judges
not_covered: Clone-only; original EdAcc recordings never evaluated; closest design to our CLONE arm without the REAL arm; no provenance axis

title: From Seeing it to Experiencing it: Interactive Evaluation of Intersectional Voice Bias in Human-AI Speech Interaction
claim: Quality-of-service vs content-level bias; accent x gender disparities in alignment and verbosity across three SpeechLLMs; voice-conversion user studies (N=24, N=19); MegaTTS3 clones
not_covered: Clone-only TTS instrument; no real recordings through models; no provenance axis

title: VoxSafeBench: Not Just What Is Said, but Who, How, and Where
claim: Two-tier safety/fairness/privacy benchmark, 22 tasks; frontier SLMs detect acoustic cues yet fail to act on them (speech grounding gap); CosyVoice3 synthesis
not_covered: Mostly synthesized audio; authors concede real-world failures may be worse but do not measure; no provenance axis

title: AHELM: A Holistic Evaluation of Audio-Language Models
claim: Ten-aspect holistic benchmark over 14 ALMs; PARADE bias set synthetically verbalized in male/female voices; Gemini 2.5 Pro tops 5/10 aspects but shows ASR group unfairness (p=0.01); ASR baselines more noise-robust than most ALMs
not_covered: Bias on TTS, fairness on real corpora, never crossed; no synthetic-vs-real comparison; no provenance axis; no detection probe

title: Voice or Stereotype? Disentangling Acoustic and Content-Based Gender in Speech-to-Speech Models
claim: Crosses Azure TTS male/female voices with stereotyped passages on five S2S models; rendered voice does not drift but gender attribution follows content (odds x1.7-24; 90% misgendering under conflict)
not_covered: TTS used deliberately as a gender-stable instrument; no real speaker; no provenance axis

title: Evaluation of Audio Language Models for Fairness, Safety, and Security
claim: Structural taxonomy of ALMs plus unified FSS framework; Qwen2-Audio vs Phi-4-multimodal differ in refusal, attack success, toxicity between audio and text; StyleTTS stimuli
not_covered: TTS-only fairness (semantic invariance under synthetic paralinguistic variation); no real recordings; no provenance axis

title: RedVox: Safety and Fairness Gaps in Speech Models Across Languages
claim: Multilingual safety/fairness benchmark on real participant voices in five languages; eight models; vulnerabilities worsen outside English and are amplified by spoken input; only 8% of releases report multilingual safety
not_covered: Real-only; criticises synthetic-voice prior work but does not measure the gap; no TTS arm, no clone, no provenance axis

title: Do LLM Decoders Listen Fairly? Benchmarking How Language Model Priors Shape Bias in Speech Recognition
claim: Nine ASR models on Common Voice 24 and Fair-Speech (~43k utterances); LLM decoders do not amplify racial bias; audio compression predicts accent fairness more than LLM scale; 12 degradation conditions
not_covered: ASR/WER only, real speech only; no audio-LLM judge or assistant behaviour; no synthetic speech; useful for WER covariate and compression framing

title: Measuring Fairness in Large Audio Language Models via Semantic-Aware Bias Estimation
claim: Mixed-effects fairness regression with semantic-embedding covariates and speaker random effect; removes spurious subgroup findings for Qwen2-Audio on LibriSpeech and AIR-Bench-Chat
not_covered: TTS only in simulation, real only in validation, never compared on same items; provenance not a covariate; statistical template to borrow

title: AudioJudge: Understanding What Works in Large Audio Model Based Speech Evaluation
claim: LAM-as-judge study (GPT-4o-Audio, Gemini-2.5-Flash): concatenation + ICL helps; multi-aspect ensemble 0.91 Spearman with humans; judges robust to Gaussian noise (85-93% verdicts stable at 1 dB SNR) but verbosity/positional biases; mixed real and TTS corpora
not_covered: Judge sensitivity to evaluee provenance never tested; no same-speaker real/synthetic pairs; no detection probe

title: Auditing Protocol-Level Shortcuts in Large Audio Language Model Judges for Speech Evaluation
claim: Six LALM judges rely on protocol shortcuts: wrong specialist labels drop emotion accuracy to <=0.10; Qwen3-Omni-Thinking picks the same A/B slot; each model-protocol pair needs a matched shortcut probe; real corpora (RAVDESS, FLEURS, BVCC, VoxCeleb1)
not_covered: Audits the protocol, not the evaluee's provenance; no real-vs-synthetic same-speaker pairing; template for our explicit probe

title: LALM-as-a-Judge: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models for Safety Evaluation in Multi-Turn Spoken Dialogues
claim: 24,000 XTTS-v2 spoken dialogues with one unsafe turn; six LALM judges; audio adds non-lexical evidence but multimodal gains are text-anchored/conservative/interfering
not_covered: TTS-only; lists synthetic speech as a limitation without measuring it; judge behaviour toward provenance untested

title: ParaPairAudioBench: Paralinguistic Pairwise Audio Benchmark for LALM-as-a-Judge
claim: 5,175 real-speech pairs over Style, Rate, Emphasis, Age, Gender; LALM judges trail humans by 32 points and fail to abstain on ties; same- vs cross-transcript conditions
not_covered: Real-only; no synthetic arm; no provenance axis

title: WavReward: Spoken Dialogue Models With Generalist Reward Evaluators
claim: Audio-LM reward model trained on TTS-rendered ChatReward-30K (GPT-4o-mini-TTS, Step-Audio clones, CosyVoice2); accuracy 53.4% to 91.5%; 120 real dialogues as OOD test
not_covered: Real dialogues are a generalisation test, not a matched comparison; reward model's treatment of provenance untested

title: ORCA: Open-ended Response Correctness Assessment for Audio Question Answering
claim: 9,663 human annotations on LALM open-ended answers; trained correctness models reach 0.91 Spearman with humans and beat Gemini 2.5 Flash as judge
not_covered: Text-side judging of LALM outputs; audio provenance plays no role

title: Assessment of L2 Oral Proficiency using Speech Large Language Models
claim: Fine-tuned Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct as L2 grader beats statistical, text-encoder and SSL baselines on Linguaskill and Speak & Improve; generalises cross-task
not_covered: Real learner speech only; trained grader; no provenance or fairness axis; deployment context for our GRADE outcome

title: Unlocking Large Audio-Language Models for Interactive Language Learning
claim: L2-Arctic-plus benchmark; instruction-tuned ALMs beat cascades on mispronunciation detection and actionable feedback
not_covered: Real learner speech only; tutor role; no synthetic speech; no provenance axis

title: VoiceBench: Benchmarking LLM-Based Voice Assistants
claim: First multi-faceted voice-assistant benchmark with real (CommonVoice, SD-QA) and Google-TTS instructions plus speaker and environment variations; Table 4: all models score higher on synthetic than real speech (VITA ~50% relative)
not_covered: Synthetic-better result is across different items and speakers, confounded with recording noise; no clone, no codec control, no detection probe

title: AudioBench: A Universal Benchmark for Audio Large Language Models
claim: 8 tasks, 26 datasets; DREAM-TTS, OpenHermes-Audio, ALPACA-Audio are TTS-rendered while others are real; no single model wins everywhere
not_covered: Never analyses TTS vs real subset performance; no provenance axis

title: HumDial-EIBench: A Human-Recorded Multi-Turn Emotional Intelligence Benchmark for Audio Language Models
claim: Argues most multi-turn benchmarks rely entirely on TTS speech; human-recorded MCQ benchmark; eight ALMs fail multi-turn emotional tracking, show text-dominance bias
not_covered: Critique of TTS benchmarks asserted not measured; no TTS arm, no same-content comparison

title: RSA-Bench: Benchmarking Audio Large Models in Real-World Acoustic Scenarios
claim: Environmental soundscapes on clean speech: perception survives but reasoning collapses; vocal-like interference worst; denoising paradox (speech enhancement often worsens ALM performance)
not_covered: Additive noise and enhancement artefacts, not codec resynthesis or synthetic provenance; no bias or judge outcomes

title: MRMAD: A Multi-Round Multi-Audio Benchmark for Evaluating Acoustic Degradation Perception in Large Audio-Language Models
claim: 18 LALMs recognise content but cannot diagnose, compare or track degradations across turns; large gap vs humans
not_covered: Asks whether models can report degradation, not whether it shifts behaviour; no synthetic provenance; parallels our probe-vs-behaviour contrast

title: Perceptually Better, Semantically Worse: Measuring Speech Enhancement Impact on LLM-Based Voice Systems
claim: Output Divergence Rate: speech enhancement changes LLM intent classification vs clean speech in every condition; MetricGAN+ doubles divergence despite better PESQ; quality metrics barely predict divergence
not_covered: Cascaded ASR+LLM; processing artefacts not synthetic provenance; no bias or judge outcomes

title: Codec-Robust Attacks on Audio LLMs
claim: Latent-space perturbations survive Opus/MP3/AAC compression (85.5% ASR on Opus, up to 100% on MP3); lossy compression is not a reliable defence
not_covered: Adversarial, not benign provenance; background for codec channel as a meaningful control
